query: What distinct aspects of food quality do reviewers focus on?

per_column.name: taste_quality
per_column.rationale: Taste/flavor is a core sensory aspect OF food quality; a genuine part-of relationship. It is arguably the most central constitutive facet of the concept.

per_column.name: convenience_usability
per_column.rationale: Ease of preparation, portability, and shelf-stability describe usability/logistics of the product, not an intrinsic aspect of the FOOD's quality. A food can be inconvenient yet high quality and vice versa, so this is a separate concept dimension rather than a facet OF food quality.

per_column.name: comparative_positioning
per_column.rationale: 'Preferred / superior / inferior to competitors' is an overall relative judgment OF quality, not a distinct constitutive aspect of it. It restates the whole concept as a ranking rather than decomposing it into a part.

judge.rationale: Only taste_quality is a true meronymic facet of food_quality. convenience_usability targets a different product concept (usability/logistics), and comparative_positioning is a holistic restatement of overall quality rather than a part of it. The three columns do not overlap much with each other (hence reasonable mutual exclusivity), but as a decomposition of food_quality they fail badly on exhaustiveness: obvious constitutive facets such as freshness, texture/mouthfeel, aroma/smell, ingredient quality, and healthiness/nutrition are entirely absent, and two of the three columns are not facets at all.
